title: Visual Studio Code Cheatsheet
description: Beginner-to-advanced Visual Studio Code reference for navigation, editing, search, IntelliSense, refactoring, Git, terminal, tasks, debugging, testing, settings, shortcuts, profiles, extensions, remote development, and troubleshooting.

sections.title: Interface & Navigation
sections.description: Use command-driven navigation to move through files, symbols, views, and history.

subtopics.title: Command Palette & Quick Open
subtopics.description: The Command Palette exposes discoverable actions; Quick Open searches files and accepts prefixes for commands, symbols, lines, and views.

tabs.label: macOS
tabs.code:
⇧⌘P / F1   Command Palette
⌘P          Quick Open file
⌘P then >   Commands
⌘P then @   Symbol in current file
⌘P then #   Workspace symbol
⌘P then :42 Go to line 42
⌃Q          Quick Open view

tabs.label: Windows/Linux
tabs.code:
Ctrl+Shift+P / F1  Command Palette
Ctrl+P             Quick Open file
Ctrl+P then >      Commands
Ctrl+P then @      Symbol in current file
Ctrl+P then #      Workspace symbol
Ctrl+P then :42    Go to line 42
Ctrl+Q             Quick Open view

callouts.title: Search Commands Before Memorizing
callouts.text: Run Preferences: Open Keyboard Shortcuts, search by command/title, and customize collisions. Shortcuts can differ by OS, layout, extensions, and keymap.

subtopics.title: Tabs, Groups & Navigation History
subtopics.description: Open files into editor groups, move between groups, and navigate location history without reopening files manually.

tabs.label: macOS
tabs.code:
⌘\          Split editor
⌘1 / ⌘2    Focus editor group
⌃Tab        Cycle recent editors
⌃- / ⌃⇧-   Back / Forward
⌘K ⌘W      Close all editors
⌘K Enter   Keep preview editor open

tabs.label: Windows/Linux
tabs.code:
Ctrl+\               Split editor
Ctrl+1 / Ctrl+2       Focus editor group
Ctrl+Tab              Cycle recent editors
Alt+Left / Alt+Right  Back / Forward
Ctrl+K Ctrl+W         Close all editors
Ctrl+K Enter          Keep preview editor open

callouts.title: Preview Tabs
callouts.text: A single-click/Quick Open result may reuse an italic preview tab. Double-click, edit, or Keep Open to pin it; configure workbench.editor.enablePreview if desired.

subtopics.title: Breadcrumbs, Outline & Symbols
subtopics.description: Navigate semantic structure from language-service symbols rather than scrolling large files.

tabs.label: macOS
tabs.code:
⇧⌘O       Go to Symbol in Editor
⌘T         Go to Symbol in Workspace
F12        Go to Definition
⌥F12       Peek Definition
⇧F12       Find All References
⌃⇧. / ⌃⇧, Next / Previous change

tabs.label: Windows/Linux
tabs.code:
Ctrl+Shift+O  Go to Symbol in Editor
Ctrl+T        Go to Symbol in Workspace
F12           Go to Definition
Alt+F12       Peek Definition
Shift+F12     Find All References
Alt+F5 / Shift+Alt+F5 Next / Previous change

sections.title: Editing, Selection & Refactoring
sections.description: Use structural operations, multiple cursors, and language-aware refactors instead of repetitive manual edits.

subtopics.title: Line & Block Editing
subtopics.description: Move, copy, delete, comment, format, indent, and join code without selecting whole lines.

tabs.label: macOS
tabs.code:
⌥↑ / ⌥↓       Move line up/down
⇧⌥↑ / ⇧⌥↓     Copy line up/down
⇧⌘K            Delete line
⌘/             Toggle line comment
⇧⌥A            Toggle block comment
⇧⌥F            Format document
⌘K ⌘F          Format selection
⌘] / ⌘[        Indent / Outdent

tabs.label: Windows/Linux
tabs.code:
Alt+Up / Alt+Down           Move line
Shift+Alt+Up / Shift+Alt+Down Copy line
Ctrl+Shift+K                 Delete line
Ctrl+/                       Toggle line comment
Shift+Alt+A                  Toggle block comment
Shift+Alt+F                  Format document
Ctrl+K Ctrl+F                Format selection
Ctrl+] / Ctrl+[              Indent / Outdent

callouts.title: Choose One Formatter
callouts.text: Multiple default formatters or format-on-save/code-action conflicts cause churn. Set language-scoped defaults and commit repository formatting configuration.

subtopics.title: Multiple Cursors & Selection
subtopics.description: Add cursors for repeated local edits, select occurrences, expand semantic selection, or use column selection.

tabs.label: macOS
tabs.code:
⌥Click        Add cursor
⌥⌘↑ / ⌥⌘↓   Cursor above/below
⌘D            Add next occurrence
⇧⌘L           Select all occurrences
⌃⇧⌘→ / ←     Expand / Shrink selection
⇧⌥ drag       Column selection

tabs.label: Windows/Linux
tabs.code:
Alt+Click                 Add cursor
Ctrl+Alt+Up / Down        Cursor above/below
Ctrl+D                    Add next occurrence
Ctrl+Shift+L              Select all occurrences
Shift+Alt+Right / Left    Expand / Shrink selection
Shift+Alt drag            Column selection

callouts.title: Use Rename for Symbols
callouts.text: Multi-cursor/text replacement cannot understand imports, scopes, strings, generated references, or language semantics. Use F2 Rename Symbol when changing an identifier.

subtopics.title: IntelliSense, Code Actions & Refactors
subtopics.description: Language extensions provide completion, parameter hints, diagnostics, quick fixes, rename, extract, organize imports, and source actions.

tabs.label: macOS
tabs.code:
⌃Space      Trigger suggestions
⇧⌘Space     Parameter hints
⌘.          Quick Fix / Code Action
F2          Rename Symbol
F8 / ⇧F8   Next / Previous problem
⇧⌘M         Problems panel
⌘K M        Change language mode

tabs.label: Windows/Linux
tabs.code:
Ctrl+Space         Trigger suggestions
Ctrl+Shift+Space   Parameter hints
Ctrl+.             Quick Fix / Code Action
F2                 Rename Symbol
F8 / Shift+F8      Next / Previous problem
Ctrl+Shift+M       Problems panel
Ctrl+K M           Change language mode

callouts.title: Refactor Preview Before Broad Changes
callouts.text: Review affected files and run project type/tests after rename or source actions, especially across generated code, dynamic usage, or multiple language servers.

sections.title: Search, Files & Workspaces
sections.description: Use scoped search and workspace configuration without hiding repository behavior in personal settings.

subtopics.title: Find, Replace & Workspace Search
subtopics.description: Editor find works in one file; Search view supports regex, include/exclude globs, replace previews, and Search Editors.

tabs.label: macOS
tabs.code:
⌘F          Find
⌥⌘F         Replace
⌘G / ⇧⌘G   Next / Previous match
⇧⌘F         Search workspace
⇧⌘H         Replace workspace
⌥⌘Enter     Replace all
⌘K C        Compare active file with clipboard

tabs.label: Windows/Linux
tabs.code:
Ctrl+F             Find
Ctrl+H             Replace
F3 / Shift+F3      Next / Previous match
Ctrl+Shift+F       Search workspace
Ctrl+Shift+H       Replace workspace
Ctrl+Alt+Enter     Replace all
Ctrl+K C           Compare active file with clipboard

callouts.title: Preview Workspace Replacements
callouts.text: Regex replacement can alter vendored/generated/binary-like text. Scope include/exclude globs, inspect diffs, and use version control before Replace All.

subtopics.title: User, Profile, Workspace & Folder Settings
subtopics.description: Settings precedence moves from defaults to user/profile, remote, workspace, folder, language, and policy/context-specific values.

table.title: VS Code Settings Scopes
rows: A remote authority such as SSH, WSL, or container
One folder in a multi-root workspace
Formatter and tab width per language

callouts.title: Do Not Commit Personal Preferences
callouts.text: Theme, font, UI layout, telemetry preference, and personal keybindings belong in user/profile settings. Commit settings required for consistent project behavior.

subtopics.title: Multi-Root Workspaces & Workspace Trust
subtopics.description: A .code-workspace file groups folders and settings/tasks. Workspace Trust restricts code execution features for untrusted content.

callouts.title: A Workspace Can Execute Code
callouts.text: Tasks, debug configs, extensions, settings, and language tooling can run repository code. Keep Restricted Mode until you trust the source and inspect configuration.

sections.title: Terminal, Tasks & Debugging
sections.description: Automate reproducible commands and debug with explicit launch behavior.

subtopics.title: Integrated Terminal & Shell Integration
subtopics.description: Use named terminal profiles, split terminals, command decorations, navigation, and detected links without confusing terminal state with editor tasks.

tabs.label: macOS
tabs.code:
⌃`          Toggle terminal
⌃⇧`         New terminal
⌘\          Split terminal (when focused/configured)
⌘K          Clear terminal
Terminal: Select Default Profile via Palette

tabs.label: Windows/Linux
tabs.code:
Ctrl+`        Toggle terminal
Ctrl+Shift+`  New terminal
Ctrl+Shift+5  Split terminal
Ctrl+K        Clear terminal (may depend on shell)
Terminal: Select Default Profile via Palette

callouts.title: Shell Initialization Affects Reproducibility
callouts.text: Environment managers and login/interactive shell behavior can differ between terminal, tasks, debugger, CI, and containers. Put required project commands/config in scripts rather than aliases.

subtopics.title: tasks.json, Problem Matchers & Compounds
subtopics.description: Tasks run builds/tests/tools with presentation, grouping, dependencies, background readiness, inputs, and problem matchers.

callouts.title: Tasks Are Shared Executables
callouts.text: Prefer package/project scripts as the source of truth so CI and other editors can run them. Review shell commands and platform assumptions before committing.

subtopics.title: launch.json, Breakpoints & Data Inspection
subtopics.description: Launch or attach a debugger with runtime, program, arguments, environment, source maps, preLaunchTask, and console behavior.

callouts.title: Do Not Commit Secrets in launch.json
callouts.text: Use ignored env files or secure runtime injection. Debug consoles, environment, variables, memory, and logs may expose sensitive values.

subtopics.title: Debug Shortcuts, Logpoints & Conditions
subtopics.description: Use conditional/hit-count breakpoints and logpoints to reduce intrusive debug edits.

codeBlocks.code:
F5          Start / Continue
F9          Toggle breakpoint
F10         Step Over
F11         Step Into
Shift+F11   Step Out
Shift+F5    Stop
Ctrl+Shift+F5 (Win/Linux) / ⇧⌘F5 (macOS) Restart

Right-click gutter → Conditional Breakpoint / Logpoint / Triggered Breakpoint

callouts.title: Pausing Production Is Risky
callouts.text: A breakpoint may halt a process/event loop. Prefer logs, traces, metrics, snapshots, or logpoints in shared/live environments and protect debug ports.

sections.title: Source Control & Testing
sections.description: Review changes deliberately and run tests through language/tool adapters.

subtopics.title: Git Changes, Stage, Commit & Graph
subtopics.description: The Source Control view displays repositories, staged/unstaged changes, diffs, commits, branches, merge conflicts, history graph, and sync operations.

tabs.label: macOS
tabs.code:
⌃⇧G       Source Control view
Open changed file → side-by-side diff
Stage selected hunks/lines from editor gutter
Command Palette: Git: Commit, Branch, Checkout, Stash, Pull, Push

tabs.label: Windows/Linux
tabs.code:
Ctrl+Shift+G Source Control view
Open changed file → side-by-side diff
Stage selected hunks/lines from editor gutter
Command Palette: Git: Commit, Branch, Checkout, Stash, Pull, Push

callouts.title: Sync Means Pull Then Push
callouts.text: Review incoming/outgoing commits before Sync. Only staged changes are committed; inspect the staged diff to avoid secrets, generated noise, or unrelated edits.

subtopics.title: Merge Editor, Timeline & Local History
subtopics.description: The Merge Editor compares base, incoming, current, and result; Timeline shows Git commits and local-history entries where enabled.

codeBlocks.code:
Resolve by understanding intended combined behavior—not Accept Both blindly.
Search every conflict marker: <<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>>
Run formatter, type checker, and affected tests after resolution.
Review final diff against both parents.
Local History is recovery help, not a replacement for Git/backup.

callouts.title: Conflict Resolution Can Compile and Still Be Wrong
callouts.text: Independent changes can violate invariants without textual conflicts. Test integration behavior and review semantic interactions.

subtopics.title: Testing View, Profiles & Coverage
subtopics.description: Test adapters discover tests and provide run/debug, status, output, filtering, continuous run, and coverage when supported.

codeBlocks.code:
Testing: Focus on Test Explorer View via Command Palette
Run/Debug icons appear in gutter for discovered tests
Use profiles to select run/debug/coverage configuration
Peek test output and navigate stack traces
Verify the same command in terminal/CI when adapter behavior differs

callouts.title: Adapter Is Not the Test Runner
callouts.text: The extension integrates an underlying runner. Keep runner configuration/scripts authoritative and diagnose differences in environment, cwd, filters, or watch mode.

sections.title: Extensions, Profiles & Remote Development
sections.description: Control privileged extension code and make environments repeatable.

subtopics.title: Extension Trust, Recommendations & Bisect
subtopics.description: Extensions can read/write files, run processes, access network, modify UI, and execute workspace code. Install minimally and inspect publisher/repository/permissions/update changes.

tabs.label: CLI
tabs.code:
code --list-extensions --show-versions
code --install-extension publisher.extension
code --uninstall-extension publisher.extension
code --disable-extensions .
code --profile "Python" .

tabs.label: Diagnosis
tabs.code:
Help: Start Extension Bisect
Developer: Show Running Extensions
Developer: Open Extensions Folder
Developer: Toggle Developer Tools
Help: Open Process Explorer

callouts.title: Recommendations Are Not Automatic Approval
callouts.text: A repository can recommend extensions. Review them before installation, especially in untrusted workspaces and development containers/remote hosts.

subtopics.title: Profiles & Settings Sync
subtopics.description: Profiles isolate settings, extensions, shortcuts, snippets, tasks, and UI state for different workflows; Sync shares selected personal configuration across signed-in devices.

codeBlocks.code:
Example profiles: Web, Python, Documentation, Demo, Empty
Export/import a profile for reproducible personal tooling
Use an Empty Profile to diagnose extensions/settings
Choose Sync categories explicitly
Never store workspace/application secrets in synced settings

callouts.title: Profiles Complement Project Config
callouts.text: Profiles customize the developer experience. Repository format/lint/build/test configuration remains the portable team contract.

subtopics.title: SSH, WSL, Tunnels & Dev Containers
subtopics.description: Remote extensions split local UI from remote extension host/files/processes. Dev Containers describe a containerized toolchain and workspace mounts/features.

callouts.title: Container Config Is Executable Supply Chain
callouts.text: Dockerfiles, features, lifecycle commands, mounts, forwarded ports, and extensions execute with developer credentials/data. Pin/review them and avoid mounting broad host secrets or Docker socket.

sections.title: Performance, Recovery & Checklist
sections.description: Diagnose editor, extension host, filesystem, watcher, language server, and project-scale issues separately.

subtopics.title: Slow Editor & Extension Diagnosis
subtopics.description: Measure startup, running extensions, processes, language-server logs, file watchers, search excludes, and remote latency before deleting configuration.

codeBlocks.code:
code --status
code --disable-extensions .
code --user-data-dir /tmp/vscode-clean --extensions-dir /tmp/vscode-exts .

# Commands: Help: Startup Performance
# Developer: Show Running Extensions
# Help: Open Process Explorer
# Start Extension Bisect

callouts.title: Exclude Generated Trees Carefully
callouts.text: Large node_modules, build, cache, virtualenv, logs, or generated trees can overload watchers/search/language servers. Use tool-specific exclusions without hiding source that must be indexed.

subtopics.title: Workspace Checklist
subtopics.description: Keep shared behavior reproducible, security boundaries visible, and shortcuts discoverable across operating systems.

codeBlocks.code:
□ Workspace is trusted only after configuration review
□ Shared settings are minimal and language-scoped where needed
□ Personal UI/theme/keybindings remain outside repository
□ One formatter/linter source of truth is configured
□ Tasks delegate to portable project scripts
□ Debug configs contain no secrets and map sources correctly
□ Git staged diff is reviewed before commit/sync
□ Test adapter matches terminal/CI runner behavior
□ Extensions are minimal, trusted, and version/update reviewed
□ Remote/container mounts, ports, features, and commands are reviewed
□ Generated directories are excluded from the right indexers
□ Performance issues are isolated with status/process/bisect tools
□ Keyboard shortcuts are checked against current OS/keymap
